Assertion (A) : India’s trade deficit, after reaching the highest level in the year 2012-13 registered continuous decline since 2013-14.
Reason (R) : There was a general decline in both P.O.L. and Non-P.O.L. deficits since 2013-14.
Codes :
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct
x: India’s merchandise trade deficit (as per the IMF Balance of Payments Manual 5) reached the highest level of US $ 195.66 billion in the year 2012-13. After that since 2013-14 (US $ 147.61 billion) it registered continuous decline till 2016-17 (US $ 112.44 billion). In this period, there was a general decline in both P.O.L. and Non-P.O.L. deficit, which played a crucial role in the declining of trade deficit. Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). However, after 2016-17 India’s trade deficit increased again and it was at US $ 160.04 billion in 2017-18 and US $ 180.28 billion in 2018-19. In 2019-20, India's trade deficit stood at US $ 157.51 billion, while in 2020-21, it was at US $ 102.15 billion. After declining for two years it increased again to US $ 189.46 billion in 2021-22 and US $ 265.29 billion in 2022-23. In 2023-24 and 2024-25 trade deficit stood at US$ 244.9 billion and US $ 286.95 billion.

s:
Consider the following statements about 'Rules of Origin':
1. Rules of Origin are the criteria needed to determine the national source of a product.
2. Rules of Origin help the custom agencies to know what regulations and fees apply to a given product.
3. These are used for the purpose of trade statistics.
4. Their importance is derived from the fact that duties and restrictions in several cases depend upon the sources of imports.
Which of the above statements are correct?
x: Rules of origin are the criteria needed to determine the national source of a product. Their importance is derived from the fact that duties and restrictions in several cases depend upon the source of imports. There is wide variation in the practice of governments with regard to the rules of origin. While the requirements of substantial transformation is universally recognized, some governments apply the criterion of change of tariff classification, others the ad valorem percentage criterion and yet others the criterion of manufacturing or processing operation. In a globalizing world it has become even more important that a degree of harmonization is achieved in these practices of members in implementing such a requirement. Rules of origin are used : ¾to implement measures and instruments of commercial policy such as anti-dumping duties and safeguard measures; ¾to determine whether imported products shall receive most-favoured-nation (MFN) treatment or preferential treatment; ¾for the purpose of trade statistics; ¾for the application of labelling and marking requirements; and ¾for government procurement. Hence, all of the given statements are correct.

After the trading parties agree on a sale of goods, the Importer requests that its bank (the Issuing Bank) issue a Letter of Credit in favour of the Exporter.
